paragraphs.text: "Until that day I cursed the angels, those uncaring lights in the sky. They rewarded my scorn with the gift of time, every year of which I've spent in devotion to their names." —Torian Sha, soul warden
"The meadow sprang up beneath me, and I perceived a path from our people's defeat to our highest glory."
Some angels protect the meek and innocent. Others seek out and smite evil wherever it lurks.
"I carry the light of truth. Do not pity those it blinds, for they never had eyes to see."
"We see clearly the error of your ways. It does not matter that you choose not to." —Urien of the Lightwielders
Giants and pit spawn attempted to topple the cathedral's pillars. The fine grit of their remains still swirls in the breeze outside.
The vanguard is skilled at waging war alone. The enemy is often defeated before its reinforcements reach the front.
"Our law prohibits capital punishment. We believe even the gravest offenders have the chance to redeem themselves." —Torian Sha, soul warden
"One's blade is only as sharp as one's conviction." —Ajani Goldmane

Her gaze prevents the petty sins and her sword punishes the rest.
Even when fate is already written, there's always time to change the names.
"Born under the sun, the first child will seek the foundation of honor and be fortified by its righteousness." —Codex of the Constellari

The spoils of war are not measured only in gold and silver.

"I'm not nearly as bothered by being outnumbered as I am by their foul stench."

Sometimes the greatest strength is the strength of conviction.
With one flap of her wings, the angel beat back the fires of war.
Her sword sings more beautifully than any choir.
"Defending the citadel is easy. I just take these big fellows outside the main gate and let the enemy take a good long look." —Mastodon keeper
"All the wizardry in the world has to pass through one small and easily sealed door." —Ajani Goldmane
Hunters of every species on the savannah, silvercoats disdain camouflage in favor of total dominance of the food chain.
"A relic donation is suggested." "The suggestion is mandatory." —Temple signs
"One does not question the size or shape of the grains of sand in an hourglass. Nor do I question the temperament of the souls under my guidance."

"Let everything return to its true nature, so that destiny may take its course."
"My motive is not vengeance but mercy. I deliver the soulless back to their severed souls."
"Courage is a proud and gleaming shield. It does not bend or hide from sight. To fight with courage, we must forge in steel."
"Truth is a straight, keen edge. There are no soft angles or rounded edges. To fight for truth, we must forge in steel."
"This is a fine suit, armorsmith. I will be safe from harm. If only you could forge rings to mail the rest of my people . . ." —Lord Hilneth

"The East Wind, an interloper in the dominions of Westerly Weather, is an impassive-faced tyrant with a sharp poniard held behind his back for a treacherous stab." —Joseph Conrad, *The Mirror of the Sea*

"The ground polluted floats with human gore, And human carnage taints the dreadful shore Fly swift the dangerous coast: let every ear Be stopp'd against the song! 'tis death to hear!" —Homer, *The Odyssey*, trans. Pope
The shapeshifter mimics with a twin's esteem and a mirror's cruelty.
"Where are we? You must learn to ask more useful questions than that."
Merfolk are best known for their subtle magic. But those who try to fight them in their own territory quickly realize that merfolk are hardly defenseless on the field of battle.
"If it has a brain, even a primitive one, we can most surely scramble it." —Garild, merfolk mage
"The key to unlocking this puzzle is within you." —Doriel, mentor of Mistral Isle
Some wizards compete not to summon the most interesting creatures, but to create the most interesting aftereffects when a summons goes awry.
"I'm one masterpiece away from ruling this pathetic world." —Saldrath, master artificer
"Your downfall was not your ignorance, your weakness, or your hubris, but your warm blood." —Heidar, Rimewind master
"All consciousness is one, separated only by a thin veil of the physical." —Jace Beleren

"Illusion is a handy but fragile medium. Use it only in a pinch, or against the dim-witted." —Jace Beleren
"Humanity has always envied the power of flight. So we took it." —Scytha, aeromage

Merfolk don't always know what they're looking for, but they're certain once they find it.
"The sharks envy our ferocity. The eels envy our cunning."
"Why fight the body when you can dominate the mind that rules it?" —Jace Beleren
Fragments of thought refract and multiply, surging in a geyser of dizzying insight.

"The construction of a defense is not accomplished by adding bricks." —Jace Beleren

Some owls house the souls of archmages of ages past.
"I give them dreams so wondrous that they hesitate to return to the world of the conscious." —Garild, merfolk mage

"The most disappointing thing about learning telepathy is finding out how boring people really are." —Teferi, fourth-level student

"I welcome it. The pasture is cleared of weeds and the wolves are frozen solid." —Lumi, goatherd

"I've never understood why so many beings lumber around on the ground. There are three dimensions, yet they use only two."

Every grave cradles a recruit.

Even the noblest of intentions and strongest of wills inevitably crumble into dust.
The wise always keep an ear open to the whispers of power.
"Stop complaining. You can rest when you're dead. Oh—sorry." —Liliana Vess
The void is without substance but cuts like steel.
"I don't know who to pity more: those who flee from my presence or the damned who can withstand it."

Oddly, no one questioned the Cabal's wisdom in hiring a zombie to work at the cemetery.
Villagers cloaked the town in magical silence, but their ears still bled.
Its victims are known by their eyes: shattered vessels leaking broken dreams.

Dark thoughts hatch and twist within the mind, straining to take wing.
The thunder of its hooves beats dreams into despair.
"Death is no excuse for disobedience." —Liliana Vess
Trained in the arts of stealth, royal assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.
"Blood is constant. Every drop I drink, someone must bleed." —Vradeen, vampire nocturnus
"You know I accept only one currency here, and yet you have sought me out. Why now do you hesitate?" —Xathrid demon
Whether the end comes swift or slow, it always comes too soon.

"In the drowsy dark cave of the mind, dreams build their nest with fragments dropped from day's caravan." —Rabindranath Tagore
"Born under the moon, the second child will stumble on temptation and seek power in the dark places of the heart." —Codex of the Constellari
"I admit, I am a creature of the city. The sights, the nightly excitement, the abundance of fine drink . . ."
"Your life will set with the sun."
The battle was over, but the carnage continued for days.
"For strength to have any meaning, there must also be . . . you."

"Rage courses in every heart, yearning to betray its rational prison." —Sarkhan Vol
They take a blood oath to die in battle. So far none have failed to fulfill the promise.
Jariad burned the midnight oil, burned through scroll after scroll, and then burned down his laboratory.
Great generals inspire by example. Goblin chieftains inspire by electrifying the barracks.

"You wish for great destruction? It is done, my master."
They fell screaming into the depths of the chasm like so many pebbles tossed down a well.
Once a barbarian army has conquered a region, their shamans summon hellhounds that keep undesirables out and prisoners in.
The mage breathed in life-giving air and breathed out death-bringing fire.
Most goblins get their turn firing the catapult, but few achieve the coveted title of Ammunition Holder.
"We are goblinkind, heirs to the mountain empires of chieftains past. Rest is death to us, and arson is our call to war."
Once he'd worked out which end of the thing was sharp, he was promoted to guard duty.

"Those who wish to invade our monastery, please take it up with my servant." —Chandra Nalaar
"Let the gray-hairs keep their ravens and drakes. My familiar will be a reflection of me: bloodthirsty, with a predator's instinct." —Taivang, barbarian warlord
"Rage is a dangerous weapon. Your enemies will try to use your anger against you. Use it against them first." —Ajani Goldmane
"Catch!"

"A flash of the lightning, a break of the wave, He passes from life to his rest in the grave." —William Knox, "Mortality"
"I don't know why people say a double-edged sword is bad. It's a sword. With two edges." —Kamahl, pit fighter
"What do they see in the throes of panic? I'm not sure I want to know." —Kezim, prodigal pyromancer
"What am I looking at? Ashes, dead man."
"Who'd want to ignite things one at a time?" —Chandra Nalaar
He raged at the world, at his family, at his life. But mostly he just raged.
"Life up here is simple. Adapt to the ways of the mountains and they will reward you. Fight them and they will end you." —Kezim, prodigal pyromancer
Days of planning. Weeks of building. Months of perfecting. Seconds of smashing.
The undisputed master of the mountains of Shiv.
Sparkmages are performance artists of sorts, but pain is the price of admission.
A typical day for a giant. A momentous event for a goat.
Keldon warriors don't need signals to tell them when to attack. They need signals to tell them when to stop.
Viashino lack the majesty of their draconic ancestors, but they lash out with equal rage and twice the spite.
Mercy is for those who keep their distance.

The druids of Mazar treat each seedcone with respect for the warrior it will become.
Each feather in its tail is a souvenir of an exotic land, a memory condensed in hue.
"Only fools and bandits use roads."

"I've seen the fully grown ones tear a baloth to gory ribbons in seconds." —Kivi, thornberry harvester
"The centaurs are truly free. Never will they be tamed by temptation or controlled by fear. They live in total harmony, a feat not yet achieved by our kind." —Ramal, sage of Westgate

The most terrifying thing about the craw wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.
He knows the name of every elf born in the last four centuries. More importantly, they all know his.
From Gaea grew the world, and the world was silent. From Gaea grew the world's elves, and the world was silent no more. —Elvish teaching
Before any major undertaking, a Cylian elf seeks the guidance of a visionary to learn the will of the gargantuan ancients.
After the oryx dies, its flesh returns to the earth, but its emerald bones remain as a tribute to the forest.
Its diet consists of fruits, plants, small woodland animals, large woodland animals, woodlands, fruit groves, fruit farmers, and small cities.
Every living thing has roots in nature. Sometimes nature gets its roots into you.
"I fear no army or beast, but only the morning fog. Our assault can survive everything else." —Lord Hilneth

Ineffable and incorruptible.
The murderous horrors of Raven's Run are legendary, but even that haunted place goes quiet when the night wolves howl.
"Do not fire upon it—it is bad luck. And a waste of arrows." —Alera Benath, Kalonian ranger

All are prey to the eyes of the wild.

The more you struggle against its coils, the tighter they get.
If you want to destroy something lifeless, make it live.

Nature grows solutions to its problems.
"This wound shall be like the chills of winter: swiftly forgotten when spring shoots rise."
Bears aren't always as strong and as mean as you imagine. Some are even stronger and meaner.
"Sometimes I wonder if our weapons and armor are a step backward." —Soron, rhox pikemaster
"We don't like interlopers and thieves cluttering our skies." —Dionus, elvish archdruid
If taken, it cuts the hand that clutches it. If given, it heals the hand that holds it.
A banner for bonds of blood or belief.
Its curve mimics the twists of life and death.
Though no longer attached to the hand, it still holds its adversary in its grasp.
The mine's riches never end, nor do the moans of the spirits doomed to haunt them.
Bright as a mirror, dark as the sea.
As the glass shattered, forgotten realities and dead memories came flooding back.

In its heart lies the secret of immortality.
"My masterpiece is complete—and so shall be my triumph." —Saldrath, master artificer
